milestone: MSCA-DN assessment framework, ticket PE-04 (Evaluator scoring contract) in plans/msca_dn_pre_evaluation_spec.md
authority: CLAUDE.md §9.4 (a decision that affects future interpretation is written to Tier 4), §9.5 (outputs reproducible from documented inputs), §12.2 (a judge verdict is Inferred, never Confirmed), §13.3 (no project fact invented: the scorer reads the candidate's own text). Tier 1: General Annexes Part 15 p. 27, scores are awarded for criteria and not for aspects, per-criterion threshold 3. Tier 2A: HE MSCA Evaluation Form V2.2 p. 2, scale 0-5 at one decimal place, weights 50/30/20, overall threshold 70 of 100. Spec §3.3, decisions 4, 5, 6, 11, 14, ticket PE-04. Not a constitutional amendment.
decision: A separate criterion-scoring stage produces the holistic 0-5 score per criterion in harness/criterion_scoring.py. The scorer reads each criterion's complete section verbatim plus the sub-sections the criterion appendix mapping declares, never an evidence pack and never the aspect findings alone. Five samples per criterion; the median is the score and the spread is labelled within-assessor repeatability. The total is S = 10E + 6I + 4Q with the per-criterion and overall thresholds both checked. The claim ledger can be withheld structurally from the cells (include_claims=False); each cell then reports grounding unassessable beside its addressal value.

appendix_resolution_granularity.reason: The mapping's rows field is prose an evaluator reads. The import renders labelled tables one pipe-delimited row per paragraph, but Table 3.1 a was flattened to label-value prose with no row boundary left, and section 8 carries no rows at all; a finer locator would fail on exactly the rows the mapping declares. The criterion input therefore appends the whole declared sub-section, which carries the declared rows and never less than them, and names every declared row beside it in the prompt. A row is resolved when its sub-section is present in some candidate section; a row whose sub-section lies in the criterion's own sections is recorded in_own_section and not duplicated.

samples_per_criterion.reason: Adopted from spec decisions 5 and 11 and ticket PE-04, which all specify N=5; no Tier 1-3 source prescribes a sample count. The library default is 5; the module command runs the stage by default and the operator may skip it.

spread_meaning.reason: Adopted from spec decision 11. Five samples from one pinned assessor over an identical prompt measure that assessor's run-to-run variability and nothing else. The label is stamped on every score and on the aggregate so a reader cannot take the spread for a decomposition of the distance from the ESR's 85.80.

score_resolution_rule.reason: The scorecard scale strings on disk say 'one decimal place' (MSCA forms) or 'half-marks may be given' (RIA/IA); a synthetic scorecard may name integers. The parser maps those three wordings; any other wording declares no resolution, the step is then not checked, and the aggregate records score_resolution null so a reader knows it was not validated. A response off a declared step fails closed rather than being rounded. The scale maximum is the top level key of the scorecard's levels and always bounds the score.

total_arithmetic.value: factor_c = weight_c * overall_max / (scale_max * sum(weights)); S = sum(score_c * factor_c)
total_arithmetic.reason: Weights 50/30/20 and the overall threshold of 70 out of 100 are on the evaluation form p. 2 (Tier 2A); the per-criterion threshold of 3 and the no-aspect-scores rule are on General Annexes Part 15 p. 27 (Tier 1), both held in the scorecard with quotes. On the DN scorecard this is 10, 6 and 4 and reproduces the ESR's 4.20 / 4.50 / 4.20 -> 85.80 (tests/harness/test_criterion_scoring.py). On the unweighted RIA scorecard (weights 1, maximum 15) the factor is 1 and the total is the plain sum the form states.

incomplete_input_is_not_scored.reason: A missing section, an unresolved appendix row or an input over the budget leaves the criterion not_scored with the reasons recorded; the judge is not called and nothing is truncated. The total and both threshold verdicts are then undetermined and the unscored criteria are named. Mirrors §12.4: a declared gap over a fabricated completion.

library_default_versus_command_default.reason: The library caller chooses whether to spend fifteen assessor calls; the operator surface runs the stage the spec specifies unless told otherwise.

value.budget_owner: assess_candidate criterion_token_budget / --criterion-budget, independent of the cells' pack budget

dn_candidate_inputs_measured.reason: Derived by measurement from the imported Tier 4 record (not a Tier 1-3 source) through build_blind_evidence and build_criterion_input on 2026-10-04 and re-derived by tests/harness/test_criterion_scoring.py::TestShippedDnCandidate. Larger than the spec's section-only table because the declared appendix travels with the section; every input is complete and every declared row resolves.

design_notes.provenance: A 0-5 score cannot travel through Judge.evaluate, whose Verdict is bounded to [0, 1]. The grader drives Judge.raw_invoke, parses each response strictly, and hand-builds a ProvenanceRecord with the score normalised by the scale maximum, the same prompt hash and the judge's own clock, so the trail stays comparable with every other harness verdict. The raw 0-5 value and the named shortcomings live on the criterion sample.
design_notes.no_cell_arithmetic: harness/criterion_scoring.py imports neither grade_expectation nor CoverageGrade, and combine_criterion_scores takes criterion scores and the scoring only. A test reads the module source to pin this.
design_notes.findings_accompany_never_replace: The cells of a criterion are appended after the section text under a header naming them an advisory machine pre-check. An input that is complete yet carries no section text is refused with the words 'findings alone'.
design_notes.two_value_cell: BlindCell.to_dict carries addressal (the coverage verdict) and grounding: in_verdict when the pack carried claim-ledger entries, unassessable when it carried none. The coverage verdict itself is unchanged; the second value is what stops an unassessable half from reading as a clean score (spec decision 4).
design_notes.criterion_budget: The criterion stage does not inherit the cells' pack budget. The pack budget is 3000 on a TPM-capped transport, under which every DN criterion would be not_scored; the stage's own budget defaults to the uncapped 32768 the spec measured against, and a caller on a capped transport lowers it knowingly.
design_notes.empty_section: A present section artifact whose sub-sections carry no text is incomplete ('carries no sub-section text to score'), because its rendered header alone would otherwise count as section text and the criterion would be scored over the findings.
